variants.text: She's the Godspeed Ginny. Somebody named her that. Four knots. Downhill. With a tailwind.
Godspeed Ginny. The name was optimistic and the boat has never once agreed with it.
Yes, Godspeed. No, I don't know who. Whoever it was never met her.
That BREEZY showing through the transom? Previous owner. Lovely woman. Terrible sailor.
You've spotted BREEZY under the paint. That was a horse. Long story. Don't ask the horse.
BREEZY? That's not a name, that's a warning about the starboard rail.
Ahead of you — KNIGHT FALLS. Forty-two cubits of thundering water. Forty-two. Cubits.
Forty-two cubits, folks. I'm required to say it. I've never been told what a cubit is.
Forty-two cubits. That's the figure in the brochure and I stand behind the brochure.
Named for a knight who went over it in armour. Or a surveyor named Knight. Or it's just 'night,' spelled wrong. Pick one.
Knight Falls. Named after Sir somebody. The chart's the only record and the chart is a rumour.
Everyone — we need to BAIL OUT. …No. Don't jump. NOT THAT KIND OF BAIL.
Time to bail! And by bail I mean the bucket. THE BUCKET. SIR.
Two ducks, one either side. Steer between them and you create a para-ducks.
Duck to port, duck to starboard. Straight up the middle and we've got ourselves a para-ducks.
Duck… duck… GOOSE.
Two ducks and a— that's a goose. That's a goose, folks.
Duck. Duck. …I had something for this.
I had shares in that mine. Of all the things I've lost in my life, it's my mine I miss the most.
Shares. In that. Bought high. I lost my mine, and I think about it most days.
I worked for White Star Line. …We'll leave it there.
Before this? White Star Line. I'd rather not go into it.
White Star. Yes. That White Star. No further questions.
I served on the poop deck. …It's a real term. It's from the French. La poupe. It's in the— stop laughing. That job stunk.
Poop deck. Raised deck aft. Nautical term, centuries old. And yes. That job stunk.
My first posting was the poop deck. I'd thank you not to make it a thing. It was already a thing. It stunk.
Off the port bow — the Calliope. Aground since '33. Same chart, same fork, same wide water and good bottom. That, folks, is a steaming pile.
She was the pride of the upper river. Now she's a steaming pile. And I do mean steaming. Boiler's still going. Nobody's told it.
That's the competition. Sorry — that WAS the competition. Steam launch, hard aground, listing. A steaming pile.

title: He read the same three words

variants.text: Same chart as mine. Same fork. He read the same three words I read. I just read them slower.
There's no version of this where I'm better than him. There's only a version where I was slower that day.
Reverse is more of a suggestion on this boat. So whatever's ahead — we're going in.
She doesn't back up. She's never backed up. We commit, or we discuss it with the bank.
Safety valve's painted shut. Pressure only goes one way. Good news — the fix is more speed.
When she starts screaming, we go faster. I know. I've stopped arguing with it.
Chart calls this stretch wide water, good bottom. Named after someone the surveyor met that season. …I hear it. I hear it now.
'Wide water, good bottom,' it says. In his handwriting. Named for a personal acquaintance. I'm going to keep going.
Hippopotamus. Four tons, opens to a hundred and fifty degrees. That's not a yawn, that's an appointment.
They look sleepy. They are not sleepy. They are the least sleepy animal on this river.
Home port's Cra-Zi. Spelled on the chart the way a drunk surveyor heard it. Everyone here says Crazy. Everyone here is wrong.
Cra-Zi. Two syllables, one hyphen, zero relation to what the locals actually call it.
That sign says NOWHERE — THREE DAYS. It said that yesterday. It'll say it tomorrow. From either direction.
You want to go to Nowhere? Everyone does. It's three days. It's always three days.
The crate? Cargo. Nothing to— the telegram said LEOPARD SPOTTED. Then SPOTTED LEOPARD. I never got a clarification.
Don't put fingers through the slats. That's not a rule, that's a eulogy.
That's the piano. It does that every wake. It's been doing it for nine miles. It's in the key of wet.
Yes, the freight is playing. No, I can't stop it. It's a piano with opinions.
Whoever's sitting on the ice — that's mission property and it's melting on your account.
The ice is for the hospital. It is not a bench. Ma'am. It is not a bench.
The river's called the Unnamed. That's not me being coy. He left the box blank and the printer set it in capitals.
You're on the Unnamed River. Named, in the end, by a man who couldn't be bothered to ask.
The Unnamed. Yes. I know. No, there isn't another one.
This water's been called the Unnamed, Sin Nombre, Rio Sem Nome, Sans Nom, and Innominata. Five languages. One word. Nobody asked.
Every outfit that came through wrote down 'unnamed' and thought they were copying the last lot. Four hundred years of that.
Innominata's on the oldest sheet, so that's the one the lawyers use. It means the same as all the others. It means nobody asked.
Some charts say Nonesuch. That's a clerk who read 'no such name' and thought it was pretty.
The Nonesuch. Sounds grand. It's a filing error with good handwriting.
The people who live here have always had a name for it. It's never been on a chart. I'm not going to be the first to spell it wrong.
There is a name. It's a good one. It's just never been official, which is a different thing from never being true.
They could fix the chart. That'd mean a second survey. Nobody's paying for a second survey while the first one still floats most boats.
Every wrong name on this water could be corrected tomorrow. It would cost money. So it won't be.
Every boat on this river runs the same chart. One survey. One season. One man with a flask and a bad ear.
This chart's wrong in the same places for everybody. Comforting, in a way.
I'm not, strictly speaking, licensed. I mention it early so it isn't a surprise later.
Licensing is a complicated subject on this river and I'd rather we enjoyed the trees.
DUCK! …the branch. THE BRANCH. Not the birds. Why are you looking at the birds.
Everybody DUCK — no, down. DOWN. Sir, there are no ducks here.
The river splits around a boulder here. I am conflicted on which way to go. Left or right.
Big rock, two channels. I am conflicted. You are looking at me like that is not a nautical term.
